title: The Cell Membrane
description: Necrosis dissolves the walls that keep cells whole. Learn about the cell's protective boundary to rebuild piece 6.

content.value: Every cell is enclosed by a thin outer layer called the CELL MEMBRANE (also called the plasma membrane). It separates the inside of the cell from its surroundings and gives the cell its shape.

The cell membrane is SELECTIVELY PERMEABLE — it acts like a gatekeeper, letting some substances in and out while keeping others out. Useful things like food and oxygen can enter, and waste can leave, but harmful materials are kept out. This control keeps the cell healthy.

CELL MEMBRANE = the cell's gatekeeper
✅ lets IN   → food, oxygen, water
✅ lets OUT  → waste products
🚫 keeps out → harmful substances

Plant cells have an EXTRA layer outside the membrane called the CELL WALL, made of a tough material. It gives plant cells strength, support and a fixed rectangular shape. Animal cells do NOT have a cell wall — only a membrane. This is a key difference you'll use later!
Both plant and animal cells have a cell membrane, but ONLY plant cells have a cell wall outside it. This is one of the most important plant-vs-animal differences.
Key Takeaway: The cell membrane is the cell's outer boundary and gatekeeper, controlling what enters and leaves. Plant cells have an extra tough cell wall outside the membrane; animal cells do not.

quiz.question: The cell membrane is described as 'selectively permeable' because it…
options: controls what enters and leaves the cell
quiz.explain: It acts like a gatekeeper, allowing some substances in and out while keeping others out.

quiz.question: Which structure is found ONLY in plant cells, not animal cells?
quiz.explain: The tough cell wall is present only in plant cells. Animal cells have just a membrane.

quiz.question: The cell wall gives a plant cell…
options: strength, support and a fixed shape
quiz.explain: The cell wall provides support and a rigid, fixed shape to plant cells.
